answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. If several quill accounts controlled by one attacker coordinate to boost a sable seller, auditors can compare their shared funding and interaction patterns, then slash the stake when collusion is proven. Creating more identities therefore does not create free influence: each one ties up capital, and detection turns that capital into a loss, while honest agents retain a haven in verifiable rules.
